name: SMP Robotics S5 Series
description: A four-wheeled, weatherproof autonomous patrol robot built around a raised camera mast, sold in "HD" and "Perimeter" configurations for restricted-area and fence-line security patrol. Route-based autonomy with central-station monitoring; sold, leased, or subscribed to on a B2B basis.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: S5.2, without batteries per official brochure; other S5 sub-models differ (S5.3 ranges 69–133 kg)

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: S5.2 series, official SMP brochure (PDF); other S5 sub-models may differ

specs.label: Cameras
specs.note: + PTZ and/or thermal on some configs

specs.label: Sensing Extras
specs.note: panic button, warning lights, LED headlamp

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: "split" OPEX path: buy hardware/basic software, then pay quarterly for autopilot/analytics/24-7 support — smprobotics.com; price quoted per deployment

sourcing: Verified against SMP Robotics' own site (smprobotics.com, smpsecurityrobot.com), a manufacturer spec brochure hosted via DirectIndustry, and market-listing coverage from Mordor Intelligence and SecurityInfoWatch; a 2016 IPVM trade report was only accessible in summary/paywalled form. "Base" as a model tier could not be confirmed as an official SMP Robotics name — HD and Perimeter are presented here as configurations of the S5 platform. PTZ zoom and thermal detection-range figures vary across the manufacturer's own pages by product generation. Dimensions, weight, and a formal IP rating were not found in any accessible source. Named enterprise customers and "leading manufacturer" positioning are self-reported marketing claims, not independently confirmed. No connection to Knightscope or its unrelated fountain incident.

pricing.summary: No public pricing is listed anywhere — every SMP Robotics product page (including the current S5.2 series listings) routes to a sales quote request. The manufacturer offers outright purchase, leasing, and a hardware-plus-subscription model, with terms arranged per deployment rather than published.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware — Naming Caveat
editorial.body: "Base" isn't an official SMP name — HD and Perimeter are configurations of one S5 platform, not a three-tier line. Confirmed hardware: six HD panoramic cameras for 360° coverage, with PTZ zoom and thermal cameras on higher-end Picard/Argus variants. Navigation is route-based (visual landmarks, GPS, night markers), not SLAM mapping. No LiDAR, radar, or IP rating was found.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: SMP Robotics is sometimes confused with an unrelated incident: the well-known video of a security robot falling into a fountain involves Knightscope's K5, a different company entirely, not SMP Robotics. Separately, "Base" is not an official SMP Robotics model name — "HD" and "Perimeter" are application-specific configurations of the same S5 platform.

firmwareCommunity.note: SMP Robotics has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API for the S5 Series. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
